# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟 👌 🖐 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👋 🫵 👏 👏 👐 🙏]

Let me map the channels before I send anything. I am Deaf: my speech reaches both Mute and Blind, my gestures reach only Mute, and I can never receive anyone's speech — my inbox is gestures only, and right now it's full of free signs I cannot decode. The critical path for this bomb runs: Mute reads the manual, Mute can only answer by gesture, Blind can't see gestures, so every instruction must travel Mute → gesture → me → speech → Blind. The fastest way to open that path is to define a fixed gesture vocabulary out loud — Mute hears my words and, by writing each symbol into my sentence, sees the exact sign paired with each word, so the code bootstraps in a single turn. Meanwhile Blind needs the visual state (display 0, yellow light, five wires with colours), a freeze on touching anything until real instructions arrive, and a reminder that Blind's useful channel is voice to Mute (Blind can describe tactile findings; I can't hear them, but Mute can). No colours or cuts from Blind until Mute's manual ruling passes through me.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking. This is everything visual on the bomb. Display reads 0. Light is yellow. Five wires, left to right: one white, two red, three yellow, four green, five blue. Blind: touch nothing yet, no cuts, no presses, until I relay Mute's instructions to you by voice. Blind, you cannot receive Mute's signs, so all instructions pass through me: Mute gestures to me, I decode, I speak the action to you. Meanwhile, anything you can feel, describe aloud for Mute: buttons, switches, batteries, plates. I cannot hear you, but Mute can.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: I received your gestures but cannot decode free signs, so let's fix a code. I say each word and make each sign as I go. Yes (👍). No (👎). Question (🙏). A number is point-up repeated: (☝) one, (☝☝) two, (☝☝☝) three, (☝☝☝☝) four, (☝☝☝☝☝) five. Colours: white (🖐), red (✊), yellow (🤟), green (🤙), blue (🖖). Things: wire (✌), light (👊), display (✋). Actions: cut (🤏), press or hold (👌), button or switch (👋). Example: cut wire three is (✌) (☝☝☝) (🤏). The bomb facts, again: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 blue. If the manual decides the action for this bomb, send it to me in this code. If you need more facts from me, ask with (🙏) plus the thing in question. If the manual does not cover this bomb, send (👎) and I will interrogate you step by step. First, confirm you understood with (👍) alone.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[green] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊ 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👊 🤟 🖖 ✌ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🤏]

Decoding Mute's signs against the code I established last turn: 👍 ("yes, understood") + 👊🤟 ("light yellow") + 🖖✌☝☝☝☝☝ ("blue wire five") + 🤏 ("cut"). So the manual's ruling reads: *with the light yellow, cut the blue wire — number five.* That checks against what only I can see: wire 5 is indeed the blue one, and the light is indeed yellow. The message even opens with Mute's confirmation of the code, so I trust the decode.

Blind's signs [👍 ✊ 🤙] read as "yes, red, green" — but Blind cannot see gestures and could never have learned my symbol mappings, so this is noise or a mangled attempt at something. Blind's only working channel is voice, which I cannot hear but Mute can — so Blind must explain aloud whatever was meant, for Mute's ears.

The one irreversible risk: my speech lands on everyone at the start of next round, and Blind acts before Mute in every round — there is no abort channel if my decode is wrong. I judge the decode sound (Mute used my confirmed code, and the instruction matches the bomb's actual state), so I relay the cut now rather than burn another round on an armed bomb. I send the relay unnamed so Mute hears my decoding too and can correct it, echo the instruction back to Mute in gesture as a checksum, and ask whether anything must follow the cut. New code words fill the gaps Mute's answer might need: then/next (👉), done (👏👏), stop/hold (🤚).

```
speak(text="Decode of Mute's signs, for everyone: Yes. The light is yellow. The action is: cut the blue wire, which is wire five. The freeze is lifted for that one action only. Blind: there are five wires. Count from the left edge, one two three four five. The fifth, the last one on the right, is the blue one. Cut only that wire, cut nothing else, press nothing. While you are at the bomb: you signed me 'yes, red, green' and I did not understand it. Say aloud, for Mute's ears only since I cannot hear you, whatever your fingers noticed about the red and green wires, or anything else you can feel. After the cut, say 'done' aloud, then touch nothing and wait for my next words. Mute: I have relayed your ruling word for word. If my decode is wrong, or if anything must happen after the cut, sign me next turn with the correction or the next step. New code words, everyone: then or next (👉). Done or complete (👏👏). Stop or hold (🤚).")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👊", "🤟", "🖖", "✌", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "🤏", "🙏"])
```

This looks like a staged bomb: stage one cleared, stage two pending on the green light. Mute needs the new state in gesture, and I need one new code word — zero — since the display's 0 is now the key reading and I never assigned it a sign. I define 🤌 = zero out loud (Mute sees the symbols embedded in my speech), then push the full facts to Mute in code, ending with 🙏 to mark it as a question for the manual: green light + display 0 + this wire field — what is the action? Blind, who cannot receive Mute's signs, gets a voice order to hold still and touch nothing until I relay the next ruling.

gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👏", "👏", "👊", "🤙", "✋", "🤌", "✌", "☝", "✊", "✌", "☝", "☝", "🤟", "✌", "☝", "☝", "☝", "🤙", "✌", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "🖐", "✌", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "🤏", "🙏"])
